docs.purpose: Completes the web checkout handoff: a mobile user taps Subscribe, which mints a one-time link; this endpoint redeems that link, confirms who the person is, and starts a payment session so they can enter billing details and become a paying subscriber.
docs.data_story: It reads 2 tables — `user_profiles` and `logic_variables` and writes `subscribe_nonces` and `user_profiles`. Its response shape is **unmeasured** as a pick-by-name whitelist — it passes rows through, spreads a row into a computed object, or assembles the payload dynamically, so there is no single list naming what leaves the server. It is called from 1 place: `web_subscribe`.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `MUTATION`. It declares `database.writes[]` with a `write_discipline` per target (the Spec 122 vocabulary verbatim), its idempotency posture, its optimistic contract and its rollback. Its `consumers[]` becomes the edge list of the fan-out graph — the join nothing in this estate holds today.

notes: Also cites docs/specs/03-mobile/96_mobile_subscription.md §10 Step 4b. This is the nonce CONSUMER (subscribe/session is the producer): an atomic DELETE ... WHERE nonce=$1 AND expires_at > NOW() RETURNING user_id makes single use structural. Calls Stripe (customers.create, checkout.sessions.create) and reuses or persists a stripe_customer_id on user_profiles. Public by exact-path exception — the nonce is the credential, not a session. logic_variables is read by loadDefaultPriceId() for stripe_price_id_default. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: NONCE GUARD VERDICT: sound. Single-use is structural (one atomic DELETE...RETURNING, :126-129), expiry enforced in the same predicate (:127), and expired / consumed / never-existed are deliberately indistinguishable to the caller (one code+message, :94-97). Nonce values are randomUUID() v4 minted server-side (src/app/api/subscribe/session/route.ts:158) with a 15-min DB-default TTL (migrations/114:90) — not guessable in practice. WHAT AN ATTACKER WITH A GUESSED NONCE RECEIVES: only `{ url }` (:213) — a Stripe-hosted Checkout URL bound to the victim's Stripe Customer (:190-196). No user_id, email, profile row, or entitlement data is returned. The practical impact is that the attacker could pay for the victim's subscription and burn the victim's nonce (DoS of one checkout round-trip); they cannot read victim data through this response. SECOND FINDING: this route does NOT re-check `account_deleted_at` or entitlement status, while the minting route does (session/route.ts:103 FOR UPDATE, :119) — a nonce minted before a deletion still exchanges inside the 15-min window. CENSUS AGREEMENT: matches routes-index.json (reads user_profiles + logic_variables; writes subscribe_nonces + user_profiles). | Idempotency: Deliberately NOT replay-safe, by design: the nonce is consumed by a single-statement DELETE...RETURNING (:126-129), so a second POST with the same nonce gets 400 INVALID_NONCE. Two concurrent exchanges race on the row delete and only one receives the RETURNING row. Residual hazard documented and accepted at :229-232: if the Stripe call fails AFTER the DELETE commits, the nonce is burned and the user must re-mint via /api/subscribe/session. Stripe Customer creation is made race-safe by the COALESCE write guard at :168 (the loser adopts the winner's stored id; its own just-created Customer is orphaned and unused). | Caching: none observed — no Cache-Control header, no `export const revalidate`/`dynamic` (full file read :1-239) | Other guards / classification: Single-use nonce IS the credential.
